text: We shipped the new dashboard yesterday after three months of work. The team is celebrating tonight.
Finally finished migrating the monolith to microservices! All 47 services are now running in production.
Completed the OAuth2 integration this afternoon. Login flow is live for all users.
Launched our mobile app on both iOS and Android today. Took eight months of dev work.
We just hit 10,000 monthly active users! Huge moment for the startup.
Shipped the v2.0 release this morning. Notes are up on the changelog.
Finished the Kubernetes migration last Friday. All 200 pods are now running on the new cluster.
We closed our Series A round this week — $12M led by Sequoia. The team is ecstatic.
Got the SOC 2 Type II certification approved today. Took 14 months of audit work.
Deployed the new payment gateway yesterday. Stripe integration is now handling all transactions.
We hit our Q3 revenue target two weeks early! $4.2M booked against a $4M goal.
Wrapped up the GDPR compliance project today. Every data flow has been audited and documented.
Finally merged the auth refactor PR! 87 files changed, two weeks of review cycles, but it's in main now.
We completed the Postgres 12 to 16 upgrade on the primary database over the weekend. Zero downtime.
Just released version 3.1 to production. All regression tests green.
We onboarded our first enterprise customer yesterday — Acme Corp signed the three-year contract.
Finished the accessibility audit remediation this afternoon. The site is now WCAG 2.1 AA compliant.
We shipped dark mode today after six months of user requests. Reception has been overwhelmingly positive.
Completed the full CI/CD pipeline overhaul last sprint. Build times dropped from 22 minutes to 4.
Delivered the Q4 feature roadmap on time — all seven planned features shipped before December.
The team just closed the 500th customer ticket this year. A new record for support.
We launched the public beta this morning! Sign-ups have already crossed 2,300.
Finished onboarding the new engineering team last week. Twelve hires across three squads, all ramped up.
We cut p99 API latency from 840ms to 120ms after last month's caching overhaul. The SRE team deployed Redis sharding and rewrote the hot paths.
Rolled out the new recommendation engine to 100% of traffic yesterday. Click-through rate jumped 31% versus the legacy collaborative filter baseline.
Our platform team successfully migrated 1.2 billion rows from MySQL to Postgres over the weekend without any customer-visible downtime.
Shipped the real-time collaboration feature to all enterprise tenants yesterday. WebSocket cluster has handled 80k concurrent editors so far without a hiccup.
We onboarded our 1,000th paying customer this morning. The sales team hit the milestone 26 days ahead of the quarterly plan.
Deployed the multi-region failover setup to production last week. Successfully drained us-east-1 during yesterday's game day with zero lost requests.
Finished rewriting the billing service in Go this quarter. Throughput went from 900 invoices per minute to 14,000, and the on-call pages dropped to zero.
The data team launched the new self-serve analytics portal on Monday. 340 internal users have already built custom dashboards in it.
We retired the last legacy SOAP endpoint on Friday. Every client is now on the gRPC gateway, closing out a two-year deprecation plan.
Released the iOS SDK 4.0 to the App Store yesterday. Binary size shrank 42% and cold-start time dropped below 200ms on our reference devices.
Completed the zero-trust networking rollout across all production VPCs last sprint. Every service-to-service call now goes through mTLS via our Istio mesh.
The infrastructure team finished migrating from Jenkins to GitHub Actions this week. We're running 8,400 workflows per day with a median duration of 3m 12s.
Shipped the new fraud detection model to production yesterday. False-positive rate fell from 3.8% to 0.9% in the first 24 hours of traffic.
We rolled out the redesigned onboarding flow to all free-tier signups on Tuesday. Day-7 activation climbed from 18% to 29% in the A/B test.
Our mobile team hit parity with the web client this release. Every feature shipped on the web in 2026 is now available on both iOS and Android.
Finished the event-sourcing rewrite of the order service last Thursday. We replayed four years of history in 11 hours without a single mismatch.
The platform team closed out the log pipeline migration to Loki this week. We're ingesting 2.3 TB per day at a third of the previous storage cost.
Landed the new query planner in staging on Monday and promoted it to production Thursday. Average query duration dropped 55% across the top 200 slow queries.
Delivered the SSO + SCIM integration to the three pilot customers ahead of the December deadline. All three enterprise contracts signed immediately after.
We wrapped up the internationalization effort last week. The product now ships in 14 locales with RTL support for Arabic and Hebrew.
Our team hit the 99.99% availability SLO for the third consecutive quarter. The error budget was barely touched even during the regional AWS incident in September.
We published the fine-tuned GLiNER model to Hugging Face yesterday. It beats the base checkpoint by 9.4 F1 points on our internal extraction benchmark.
Our research team reproduced the DeepMind paper's key results this week after four months of work. The replication matched their reported scores within 0.3% on all three tasks.
Passed the MLPerf inference benchmark target last Friday — our optimized kernels hit 28,000 tokens/second on a single H100, above the 25k goal.
The lab submitted our paper on retrieval-augmented memory to NeurIPS yesterday, closing out eight months of experiments and three rounds of internal review.
We defended the thesis proposal this morning and passed. The committee signed off on all three research directions without revisions.
Our agent hit a new high score of 87.3 on SWE-Bench Verified yesterday, up from 74.1 on the previous checkpoint. Evaluation suite ran clean.
Completed the peer review revisions on the ICLR submission last night. Camera-ready version has been uploaded to the conference system.
We finished the ablation sweep across all 12 model variants over the weekend. The full results table is now in the appendix of the draft.
Got the IRB approval for the longitudinal study this morning after the third amendment. Data collection starts Monday with 240 enrolled participants.
Our preprint crossed 500 citations this week, two years after posting on arXiv. It's now our most-cited paper.
We closed out the replication study this quarter — all four target results reproduced within the reported confidence intervals using only open-source tooling.
The team finished benchmarking the new attention kernel against FlashAttention-3 yesterday. We matched their throughput at 4k context and beat it by 12% at 32k.
Shipped the research codebase as a public repository on Tuesday. It's already picked up 1,200 stars and nine external contributors filed PRs.
We completed the human evaluation study last week. 142 annotators graded 3,000 outputs and inter-rater agreement landed at kappa 0.81.
Our lab hit the $2M grant milestone yesterday when NSF confirmed the award. Funding covers three postdocs and compute for the next four years.
We presented the poster at ACL this afternoon. Got great engagement, including a detailed Q&A with one of the reviewers who was initially skeptical in the meta-review.
Finalized the open-source license on our benchmark suite last night and pushed the v1.0 tag. Seven external labs have already started running against it.
The workshop paper got accepted at EMNLP this morning with no required changes. Two of three reviewers gave it a strong accept.
We finished training the 13B model checkpoint last Thursday. Final loss converged to 2.14, below the 2.2 target we set at the start of the run.
Our team reproduced the Chinchilla scaling law curves on our internal pretraining corpus this month. Fit parameters are within 4% of the original paper.
The indexer now stores 42 million documents with sub-linear query growth after last month's partitioning work. We validated the scaling behavior against the production query log on Tuesday.
After three quarters of iteration, our team brought the recommendation service's P95 latency under 50ms across all five regions, closing out the OKR we set in January.
We successfully decommissioned the last Oracle database yesterday. The migration team spent 14 months moving 23 schemas and 180 stored procedures to Postgres.
Our pipeline now ingests 4.2 billion events per day with under one minute of end-to-end lag, a result the data platform team delivered last sprint after the Kafka 3.6 upgrade.
The authentication rewrite the identity squad finished this week moved every tenant off the legacy session store, and all 12 million active sessions were migrated without a single forced logout.
After six months of effort, the storage team hit the 99.999% durability target in production. The final validation run on Monday closed out the last remaining gap from the Q2 audit.
The graph service now spans 18 billion edges with 11ms median traversal time — a number the team beat their Q1 commitment by 40% on during last week's load test.
Our observability stack now retains 90 days of high-cardinality metrics across every service, a capability the platform team delivered after rewriting the Prometheus remote-write layer in Rust.
The payments team closed out PCI DSS Level 1 certification this morning after the external assessor signed off on the final control. Eleven months of audit work, done.
Every customer-facing service now runs behind the new WAF the security team rolled out in phases from August through December. The final tenant cutover completed on Friday.
The checkout flow now completes in under 800ms at P95 worldwide — the frontend team hit that target on Monday after the edge-rendering migration wrapped up in the Paris and São Paulo POPs.
We finished rewriting the entire ingestion path in Rust this quarter. The new service handles 3x the load at 40% of the memory, and the old Python workers were removed from the repo yesterday.
The ML platform now serves 2,400 models in production after the autoscaling rollout the team completed last week. Tail latency under load held steady at 18ms across the benchmark suite.
Every line of our search stack now runs on the in-house vector database the storage team shipped in November. The final Elasticsearch cluster was torn down this morning.
The orchestration layer we've been building since last spring now drives 100% of deploy traffic. The SRE team promoted it out of canary on Thursday after a full week of zero-regression dashboards.
Our model quantization effort shipped to production last week. The 8-bit version preserves 99.2% of the full-precision accuracy while cutting inference cost by 58%.
The localization team wrapped up the right-to-left layout rework for the entire product surface this sprint. 3,100 UI strings and 420 component layouts passed the final QA sweep on Wednesday.

The compliance engineering team delivered the full audit trail pipeline last week. Every write to a customer record now produces an immutable, cryptographically signed log entry, closing the open gap from the Q3 pen test.
After nine months of performance work, the frontend bundle is now 340 KB gzipped — a 62% reduction that the web platform team hit on Friday when the last code-split landed in main.

The team finished migrating every internal tool off the shared auth cluster this week. Forty-seven tools now authenticate through the new federated gateway, and the old cluster was retired Monday morning.
Our BFS traversal on the knowledge graph now runs in 380ms for the 2-hop query set that used to take 6.1 seconds, a result the core team delivered after the index rework shipped last sprint.
The recovery path we built during the October outage remediation has now been exercised cleanly in three successive game days. The reliability team closed the post-incident action plan on Friday.
After eighteen months of training, I ran the New York City Marathon last Sunday in 3:47:12, two minutes under my goal. It was my first marathon.
We closed on the house in Portland yesterday — 1,840 square feet, three bedrooms, and a detached garage. First home either of us has owned.
I walked across the stage on Saturday and picked up the diploma. Six years of night classes while working full-time, and the bachelor's in computer science is finally done.
My wife gave birth to our daughter at 4:18am on Tuesday. She weighed 7 pounds 3 ounces, and we're all home now.
I finished the Pacific Crest Trail last Thursday — 2,653 miles over 142 days, starting at the Mexican border in April.
Paid off the last $1,870 of the student loan this morning. Eleven years of monthly payments since graduation, finally zero balance.
Got sober yesterday, five years to the day. I haven't had a drink since the morning of April 14th, 2021.
Passed the bar exam on the third attempt this cycle — results came in last Friday. Starting at the firm on the 21st.
Got married in Kyoto on October 3rd. Forty-two guests flew in, and the ceremony at Shiramine Shrine lasted about ninety minutes.
Adopted the dog we'd been fostering — papers were signed yesterday morning. Bailey has officially been ours for two days now.
Defended my dissertation this afternoon and passed with no revisions. The committee signed the approval form at 3:40pm and I'm officially a PhD.
Quit smoking a year ago today. Haven't touched a cigarette since April 15th, 2025, after thirteen years of the habit.
Finished my first novel last night — 94,000 words, three years of drafting, and the final chapter went in at 11:42pm. The manuscript is now with the agent.
Summited Denali on May 28th after a 19-day push from base camp. The whole rope team made it up and back down without frostbite.
Hit $100,000 in the retirement account this month, eight years after opening it. Milestone I wasn't sure I'd reach before forty.
Got my private pilot's license on Friday. 67 logged hours, the checkride was cleaner than my practice flights, and the DPE signed the temporary certificate that afternoon.
Lost the 85 pounds. Started in March 2024 at 278, stepped on the scale this morning at 193, and the doctor took me off the blood-pressure meds last week.
Moved into the new apartment on the 1st — first place I've lived alone. Three flights of stairs, 520 square feet, and entirely mine.
Finally got my US citizenship yesterday at the naturalization ceremony in Seattle. Seventeen years after arriving on an F-1 visa in 2009.
Swam the English Channel on August 12th — 21 miles in 13 hours and 44 minutes. Two years of 4am training sessions paid off.
Celebrated twenty years at the company this week. They threw a small lunch for me on Thursday, and I got the crystal paperweight that goes with the anniversary.
Completed chemotherapy yesterday — final infusion was at 2pm. Oncologist says the scans are clean, and I ring the bell on Friday.
Our cohort onboarded its 10,000th nonprofit to the grants portal this week. It took four years of partnerships to reach that number, and the ops team hit the target on Monday morning.
The distributed tracing system now captures every span across all 312 services in the production fleet, closing out a rollout the observability team started back in March.
The new consensus protocol we built in-house has now handled every write in the primary region for thirty consecutive days without a single leader election failure.
Our on-call burden dropped below one page per engineer per week this month, a threshold the reliability team hit after the noisy-alert cleanup they finished in late March.
The new schema registry went from prototype to serving 100% of internal producers this quarter. The data platform team closed the migration on April 9th with the last Avro-to-Protobuf cutover.
After three years of effort, the team landed full WebAssembly support in the runtime. The last unsupported SIMD instruction shipped in the 2026.2 release two weeks ago.

We finished the migration of every customer from the legacy billing plan this sprint. All 38,400 accounts are now on the new metered pricing model, and the old plan code was deleted from the repo on Wednesday.
